project: Federal Procurement Integrity Observatory - cycle-3 thin slice: threshold shifts (a market-level screening indicator, not an accusation about anyone)
target: Whether the pile-up of civilian purchase orders and definitive contracts just under the simplified acquisition threshold keeps following the threshold ($250,000 until 2025-09-30, $350,000 from 2025-10-01) and how far the micro-purchase reporting step has moved ($10,000 -> $15,000), in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027.
resolution_source: USAspending.gov contract transactions (Advanced Search transaction download), civilian top-tier agencies (all except the Department of Defense), award types B and D, base actions (modification_number 0)
resolution_rule: Run scripts/12_resolve_threshold.py on a snapshot taken on or after 2027-02-15. It downloads the period, keeps base actions, and recomputes the three quantities with the estimator frozen in scripts/bunching_lib.py (bins, window, exclusion zone, polynomial degree, Poisson fit). A forecast 'hits' if the actual value lies inside the 80% interval; it 'beats the baseline' if its absolute error is smaller than that of the persistence baseline.

quantities.name: bunching_ratio_350K
quantities.definition: observed / counterfactual number of civilian PO+definitive-contract base actions with base-and-all-options value in the four $5,000 bins up to $350,000 (bins are right-closed), counterfactual = degree-5 Poisson polynomial fitted outside (T-20K, T+10K] over the window in SPEC of scripts/bunching_lib.py

quantities.name: bunching_ratio_250K
quantities.definition: observed / counterfactual number of civilian PO+definitive-contract base actions with base-and-all-options value in the four $5,000 bins up to $250,000 (bins are right-closed), counterfactual = degree-5 Poisson polynomial fitted outside (T-20K, T+10K] over the window in SPEC of scripts/bunching_lib.py

quantities.name: po_share_10_15K
quantities.definition: among civilian purchase-order base actions with federal_action_obligation in ($10,000, $20,000], the share that lie in ($10,000, $15,000]

method: Point forecast = mean of the estimates for FY2026 Q3 and Q4, the two latest quarters after the 2025-10-01 threshold change (quarterly estimates in results/threshold_quarterly_bunching.csv). The pile-up at $350K rose every quarter since the change (1.51, 1.65, 1.89, 2.17) and the one at $250K fell (1.50, 1.24, 1.28, 1.18); the micro-purchase share fell (0.49, 0.45, 0.36, 0.36). Interval half-width = 1.28 * sqrt(sampling_se^2 + level_se^2) where sampling_se is the bootstrap error of the two most recent first-quarter samples (small, and depressed by the Oct-Nov 2025 shutdown in FY2026 Q1), and level_se allows for drift (0.30 and 0.15 ratio points; 0.03 for the share).
known_limitations: Only four quarters exist since the change and the trend may not have stopped; the interval allows for drift but not for a new policy shift.
FY2027 Q1 data may be revised by late reporting; the earliest scoring date leaves six weeks after quarter end.
Bunching is a market-level indicator; legitimate scoping to fit simpler rules produces the same signature. No office or person is implicated.
The Department of Defense is excluded (its data are published with a 90-day delay).
Poisson-polynomial counterfactuals are sensitive to specification; the specification is frozen in scripts/bunching_lib.py.
